mechanism_posthoc.finding_1: optimizer DOES respond to w_stab: optimized CDSs differ across weights (6/6 pairs differ in 19/24 weight-pair cells)
mechanism_posthoc.finding_2: proxy moves the WRONG way: median terminal-window proxy mfe/nt goes -0.1405 (w=0) -> -0.1153 (w=1.0), i.e. LESS stable as w_stab rises — the proxy windows overlap the junction windows, and the junction-accessibility term (-0.5*|j_mfe|) dominates the stability reward in the SAME windows
mechanism_posthoc.finding_3: true full-construct cost is flat per cell across all weights and comparable to v1 per-cell costs — the global stability cost is generated by long-range rearrangements invisible to 160-nt terminal windows
mechanism_posthoc.conclusion: local terminal-window proxies are structurally incapable of controlling global stability (double-count the junction term, blind to global rearrangements). The stability trade-off is not controllable post-hoc; it belongs inside the generative tool at design time (e.g. LinearDesign's global CAI-MFE balance + junction term at generation time).

implication: NO-GO per pre-registration: no weight achieves the GO criteria. Per docstring, the Pareto curve is documented as-is. Integration into FullLengthMrnaDesignWorkflow as a post-hoc option is NOT warranted; revisit E4 executor plan (design doc §3 E4 dependency).
